Same construction as above: attention = weekly count vs own trailing 4 weeks; tone = count-weighted weekly sentiment; EPS revision, rating drift and short interest identical.

Lead or lag? Cross-correlation of each signal with weekly returns, 2024-01-05 → 2026-08-28

The forward-IC tables above cannot tell a leading signal from sentiment that simply follows price. This section does. For each signal measured at the end of week t, the bars show the rank correlation with the universe-relative return of week t+k: k<0 is the return that happened before the signal (sentiment reacting to price), k=0 is the same week (coincident), k>0 is the return that came after (the signal leading). Weekly returns do not overlap, so each bar's t-stat is honest. The partial IC column repeats the k=+1 test after controlling for the past 4 weeks' return: a signal that is only re-packaged momentum goes to zero there.
noneclassified leading (|IC| at k=+1..+2 is significant and at least as large as the coincident/lagging side)
BBG Twitter publication count vs trailing 4w, BBG Twitter sentiment, BBG Twitter sentiment change vs trailing 4w, BBG news sentiment, BULL compositeclassified coincident (moves with the same week's return)
BBG news publication count vs trailing 4w, EPS revision, Analyst rating drift, HOT compositeclassified lagging (mostly reacts to the return that already happened)

The table behind the bars — IC by lag, partial IC at k=+1 after momentum, verdict

Reverse direction — does this week's return predict next week's signal?

A large positive number here is the signature of a lagging signal: price moves first, the crowd talks about it afterwards.

Double sort — signal tercile inside each momentum tercile → mean forward 15-day relative return

Rows = past-4-week return tercile, columns = signal tercile. If the signal only proxies momentum the columns look alike inside each row; if it adds information the right column beats the left within rows.

Earnings event windows — 1,045 prints, Jan-2024 → Aug-2026

For every earnings announcement of the 99 names: signals measured over the 10 calendar days before the print (vs the prior 30 days as baseline) and outcomes measured from the last close before the print: reaction (to the next close), 15 days total, and drift (from the post-print close to day +15). All returns are relative to the equal-weight universe. IC = Spearman across events; Q5−Q1 = top minus bottom quintile mean outcome. Own-corpus signals exist from 2026-05-01 (n≈100), sell-side from 2026-01-30.

Methodology, sources and what is deliberately left out
Own tweet corpus
twitter-briefing routine (daily 09:00, twitterapi.io) → E:\.claude\data\twitter-briefing\tweets.sqlite. ~440 handles curated by the briefing skill (semis, micro, AI/ML, hedge funds, wires). Retweets dropped; replies and quotes kept. Dense coverage from May 2026 only — earlier months are not backfilled (decision 2026-09-02).
Bloomberg track
bdh fields TWITTER_SENTIMENT_DAILY_AVG, TWITTER_PUBLICATION_COUNT, TWITTER_POS/NEG_SENTIMENT_COUNT, NEWS_SENTIMENT_DAILY_AVG, NEWS_PUBLICATION_COUNT since 2023-12 for every name with a Bloomberg line. Bloomberg's own classifier; coverage of non-US lines is thinner.
Ticker mapping (own corpus)
Cashtag ($NVDA) or company-name alias (case-sensitive for ambiguous names: Apple, Meta, Oracle, Arm Holdings, Samsung…). A tweet naming N tickers gives each 1/N (N≤3) or 0.25/N (lists). Private names (OpenAI, Anthropic, Cerebras) excluded — no price.
Attention (HOT)
log((count this week + 0.5) / (mean of trailing 4 weeks + 0.5)), curated and wire (or BBG Twitter and BBG news) separately; each z-scored across names; HOT = mean of the two z. Needs ≥2 prior weeks.
Tone
Own corpus: finance lexicon (~80 bull / ~100 bear stems, 3-word negation flip), per tweet in [−1,1]; weekly engagement-weighted mean, shrunk by n/(n+5). Not LLM-scored — the upgrade path. Bloomberg track: count-weighted weekly mean of the daily sentiment score.
BULL composite
Mean z of: tone, tone change vs trailing 4w, Bloomberg BEST_EPS (1BF) 4-week % revision (|Δ|>25% dropped as fiscal-roll artefacts), BEST_ANALYST_RATING 4-week drift (Bloomberg track adds news sentiment). Short interest is a separate crowding leg.
Returns & horizons
PX_LAST Friday closes, local currency; forward 1w / 15d / 4w (calendar days); backtest uses universe-relative returns. Non-USD names carry FX noise in raw returns. Forward windows overlap week to week, so treat t-stats as indicative.
Sell-side e-mails
Outlook desktop over COM, store-side DASL filter on ~65 broker sender domains, subject + body (bodies fetched by EntryID, URLs stripped, text cut at the first disclaimer marker, first ~6k chars scanned for tickers; tone and actions read in ±250-char windows around each ticker mention; rating changes from "Rating: From X to Y" / "upgrade to" patterns, PT changes from "Price target: From $A to $B" / "PT to $B from $A", estimate direction from "raising/lowering estimates"), all mail folders except deleted/junk/sent. Mailbox retention starts 2026-01-31, so this leg covers Feb-2026 onward. Ticker mapping = cashtag / alias / ticker token (short tickers need parentheses or a "US" suffix); tone = the same lexicon; actions = upgrade/downgrade/PT raise/cut regex on the subject; noise (webinars, invites, corporate access) dropped. Blast e-mails naming N tickers weight 1/N.
Lead/lag test
Cross-correlation function on weekly non-overlapping universe-relative returns: IC(k) = mean over weeks of Spearman(signal at week t, return of week t+k), k = −4…+4. Partial IC = Spearman partial correlation controlling for the past-4-week return. Double sort = tercile × tercile on the same week. Verdict rule: leading if |IC(+1,+2)| is significant (|t|≥2) and ≥60% of the larger of the coincident/lagging sides; lagging if the k<0 side dominates; coincident if k=0 dominates. Signals built with a trailing window (attention, tone change, EPS revision) mechanically embed weeks t−4…t, so their k<0 bars partly reflect construction.
Event windows
Announcement dates, times and EPS actual/estimate from Bloomberg EARN_ANN_DT_TIME_HIST_WITH_EPS. After-close prints (or no time) use the day's close as base; pre-market prints use the prior close. Pre-window = 10 calendar days, baseline = the 30 days before that. Outcomes relative to an equal-weight index of the 99 names. |surprise| > 100% and |EPS revision| > 25% dropped as artefacts.
